rv.q: There is an odd mix of tones and numerous fanciful or philosophical digressions. It’s not wrong to call “The Potluck” a mess. As I wrote about “Futurity,” Alvarez’s 2015 musical : “What it is exactly is hard to sum up or to pin down.” But I found “The Potluck” extraordinary, and devastating.
Alvarez tells the story in seemingly unrelated but fascinating dollops of information that coalesce when they sings 'The Ballad of the 5'.
It doesn't bode well for audiences embarking on a two-hour, 30-minute musical that the writer isn't even that interested in.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this unconventional musical about the Greensboro Massacre, with praise for its personal approach but concerns about its structure and execution as it focuses more on the writer's anxieties than the historical tragedy itself.
